title: Company-wide policies and processes - central reference
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:

This page is the canonical, company-wide reference for policies and standard processes that apply across Redwood Inference. It consolidates guidance and templates for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and commonly used internal templates. Use the links in the Related Resources section to navigate to deeper team-level playbooks.

Purpose and scope:

- Purpose: Provide a single, searchable source of truth for employees, managers, and auditors describing who owns decisions, the required approvals, and step-by-step procedures for common cross-functional operations.
- Scope: Applies to all employees, contractors, and vendors who perform work for Redwood Inference. Exceptions must be documented and approved by the owner_team and security/finance as applicable.

Ownership and governance:

- Document owner: people-ops (Asha Patel).
- Governance cadence: Quarterly review by people-ops, finance-legal, and security teams; ad-hoc updates as regulatory or business changes require.
- Escalation path: Team manager -> People Ops -> Head of People Ops -> Legal/Finance/Security as required.

1) Access and permissions (RBAC and onboarding/offboarding)

Overview:
- Access to services and resources is controlled via role-based access control (RBAC) and least privilege principles. The security team maintains the global RBAC mapping and regularly audits high-risk roles.

Key roles & responsibilities:
- Requester: employee or manager initiating access.
- Approver: direct manager for standard accesses; security or service owner for privileged accesses (see Privileged Access below).
- Access Owner: service or data owner responsible for periodic access reviews.
- IT/Identity team: implements provisioning and revocation through our identity provider (IdP).

Privileged access definitions and controls:
- Privileged roles: any role granting write access to production, admin rights to cloud accounts, KMS/HSM access, or sensitive data stores (PII, customer secrets).
- Approval flow: Privileged request -> Manager approval -> Security review -> People Ops notification -> Provisioning.
- Time-bound access: Temporary privileged access must include an expiration and justification; maximum default duration = 7 days unless extended by security.

Onboarding and offboarding process (high level):
1. New hire request submitted via HRATS (onboarding form) with required resource list.
2. Manager confirms required accesses during the offer acceptance call.
3. IdP automation provisions baseline accounts and group membership within 24 hours of user account activation.
4. Access Owner conducts first access review within 30 days of hire.
5. Offboarding: Manager or HR flags termination -> IdP disables access immediately on termination event; optional step to retain read-only account per retention policy (must be approved).

Access reviews and audit:
- Frequency: Quarterly role review for all production-facing roles; monthly review for privileged role lists.
- Audit artifacts: approvals and access logs are retained for 3 years or per compliance evidence requirements.

2) Change management (infra, service, and data schema changes)

Principles:
- All production-affecting changes require a documented change request, risk assessment, and a rollback plan.
- Emergency changes allowed but must be post-facto reviewed within 24 hours.

Change categories and approval matrix:
- Low-risk: Configuration or documentation changes with no user-visible impact. Approver: Service owner.
- Medium-risk: Non-breaking infra changes, non-production schema changes. Approver: Service owner + Platform lead.
- High-risk: Production-deploying code changes, DB schema migrations, infra changes that can affect latency/availability. Approver: Service owner + Platform/Infra lead + SRE on-call review.
- Critical emergency: P1 incident fix. Approver: Incident commander + SRE lead, must be followed by a post-incident change review.

Change request template (required fields):
- Title, owner, change window, systems affected, risk level, rollback plan, test plan, communications plan, monitoring/verification steps, approvers.

Standard change process (step-by-step):
1. Create change request in the Change Management tracker (Jira project: CHG).
2. Attach runbook, migration scripts, and test evidence.
3. Notify stakeholders 72 hours before planned window for medium/high risk.
4. Execute in staging and run automated smoke tests.
5. For production, deploy using the approved rollout policy (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% or as configured per service).
6. Monitoring: verify SLO indicators for at least 30 minutes post-deployment.
7. If regression detected, execute rollback and open post-change review.

Emergency change process:
1. Declare emergency in incident channel.
2. Implement workaround/fix.
3. Document change retrospectively and submit change request within 24 hours.
4. Conduct review with stakeholders within 72 hours.

3) Data management (classification, handling, retention, backups)

Data classification levels:
- PUBLIC: Non-sensitive, can be published externally.
- INTERNAL: Company-internal operational data, includes most documentation and dashboards.
- CONFIDENTIAL: Customer data, non-public business info. Limited access.
- SENSITIVE: PII, secrets, regulated customer data. Strict handling and encryption required.

Handling requirements: 
- Encryption: All CONFIDENTIAL and SENSITIVE data must be encrypted at rest and in transit (KMS-managed keys).
- Access approvals: Requests for CONFIDENTIAL/SENSITIVE data require business justification and an assigned Data Owner approver.
- Data sharing: External data sharing requires a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) reviewed by Legal.

Retention and deletion:
- Default retention: Internal docs = 7 years, logs = 1 year (unless longer required by compliance), backups = 30 days (hot) + 180 days (cold).
- Deletion requests: Data subject requests or legal hold must be routed to Legal and Data Privacy lead.

Backups and disaster recovery:
- Backups: Daily incremental with weekly full snapshot for critical systems. Backups are stored in encrypted form across regions.
- Recovery targets: RTO (critical systems) = 4 hours; RPO = 1 hour for critical services. Non-critical systems use a 24 hour RTO/RPO.

4) Procurement and expenses

Procurement thresholds and approvals:
- Low-value purchases (< $1,000): Team lead approval.
- Mid-value ($1,000 - $25,000): Department head + Finance approval.
- High-value (>$25,000): VP-level approval + Finance and Legal review; RFP recommended for > $100,000.

Preferred vendor process:
1. Submit purchase request in ProcureX with supporting vendor quotes and SOW if applicable.
2. Finance validates budget and issues PO.
3. Procurement onboards vendor into our vendor registry and collects tax/W9 and insurance certificates.

Expense policy highlights (employees):
- Acceptable expenses: reasonable travel, training, approved software seats, and business meals.
- Per diem: Follow published per-diem tables by region (link in Templates).
- Reimbursement: Submit receipts in Expensely within 30 days. Missing receipts over $75 require manager justification.

Payment terms and invoices:
- Standard payment terms: Net 30 unless contract specifies otherwise.
- Invoices > $10,000 require three-way match (PO, goods received, invoice).

5) Vendor management

Vendor lifecycle steps:
1. Evaluation: Security, privacy, and finance run initial vendor assessment.
2. Contracting: Legal negotiates terms, includes SLA, data protection addenda, and termination clauses.
3. Onboarding: Procurement registers vendor and collects required compliance artifacts.
4. Ongoing review: Quarterly performance review for strategic vendors, annual security review for vendors with access to CONFIDENTIAL/SENSITIVE data.

Vendor risk levels and controls:
- Low risk: SaaS with no access to customer data. Controls: basic contract and PO.
- Moderate risk: Vendor processes INTERNAL data or integrates with internal tooling. Controls: security questionnaire and periodic review.
- High risk: Vendors processing SENSITIVE or CONFIDENTIAL data or with privileged access to systems. Controls: Data Processing Agreement (DPA), SOC2 or equivalent report, encryption, and quarterly audits.

Termination & offboarding checklist:
- Revoke all credentials and access, ensure return or destruction of customer data, terminate integrations, and confirm final payments. Document completion in the vendor record.

6) Travel policy (business travel and remote work travel guidelines)

Booking and approvals:
- All business travel must be approved by the employee's manager before booking. International travel also requires Geo Risk sign-off for designated regions.
- Use TravelPortal for booking to ensure preferred vendor rates. Exceptions must be justified.

Allowed classes and limits:
- Domestic coach/standard economy for flights under 6 hours. Premium economy or business requires VP approval.
- Hotel: mid-range business hotels; approvals required for boutique/luxury hotels.
- Ground transportation: rideshares or standard taxis; car rentals booked via TravelPortal.

Expense reconciliation:
- Submit itemized receipts and travel itinerary in Expensely within 10 business days of return.
- Per-diem applies where local regulations or extended travel make itemized receipts impractical.

Traveler safety and insurance:
- Redwood provides business travel insurance for approved international travel. Register trips in the TravelSafety tool.

7) Internal templates and common artifacts

This section centralizes templates to reduce rework. Available templates (links in Related Resources):
- Access request template (required fields: resource, justification, approver).
- Change request template (CHG Jira issue template).
- Vendor intake checklist and security questionnaire.
- Expense report template and per-diem tables.
- Standard contract addenda (DPA, SLA language).
- Travel authorization form.

How to request new templates:
1. Submit a template request to people-ops via the Templates intake form.
2. People-ops reviews for legal/finance/security dependencies and publishes a draft.
3. Solicit feedback from stakeholders; finalize and add to the Templates library.

Compliance and evidence collection:
- Maintain an audit trail for all approvals: electronic approvals are the default (IdP logs, Jira approvals, ProcureX records).
- Retention of approval artifacts follows the Data Management retention table above.

Training and awareness:
- People-ops runs mandatory annual training covering: access policies, data handling, expense policies, and vendor onboarding requirements.
- New hires receive required policy reading during onboarding; completion tracked in the LMS.

Appendix A - Quick checklists (copyable) :

Onboarding access checklist:
- [ ] Offer accepted and HRATS record created
- [ ] Baseline IdP provisioning completed
- [ ] Manager-approved additional access requests submitted
- [ ] Access Owner review scheduled within 30 days

Change deploy quick checklist:
- [ ] CHG request created and approved
- [ ] Runbook and rollback documented
- [ ] Stakeholders notified
- [ ] Smoke tests passing in staging
- [ ] Monitoring configured for post-deploy verification

Expense submission quick checklist:
- [ ] Receipts attached
- [ ] Correct cost center and project code selected
- [ ] Manager approval included

- Finance: finance-ops@redwoodinference.example.com
- Security/Identity: security-idp@redwoodinference.example.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwoodinference.example.com

If you need a printable version of any template or a walkthrough session, contact people-ops to schedule a working session.
